text:
devon: Quick FYI — after the Triton 2.3 runtime roll to staging we see consistent perf regressions for attention when seq_len > 2048. Fusion/CUDA kernels (legacy) beat the Triton variant on SM90 in our microbench. Posting numbers and small profiles. :eyes:
sasha: Can you paste the raw numbers + the config you used?
devon: Sure — microbench command: `./bench_attention --model gpt-j --seq 4096 --bs 1 --warm 10 --iter 50 --impl triton|cuda`

Results (tokens/sec):
```
model,arch,seq,bs,impl,tokens_per_sec,rel_to_best
gpt-j,sm90,2048,1,cuda,1450,1.00
gpt-j,sm90,2048,1,triton,1400,0.97
gpt-j,sm90,4096,1,cuda,980,1.00
gpt-j,sm90,4096,1,triton,760,0.78
gpt-j,sm80,4096,1,cuda,930,1.00
gpt-j,sm80,4096,1,triton,900,0.97
```
devon: TL;DR — triton slowdowns ~22-25% on sm90 at long sequence lengths; sm80 shows much smaller gap.
omar: Huh. Did you build Triton kernels with CUDA 12.2 and sm90 arch flags? Any differences in nvcc flags or math libs?
devon: Build flags: `-O3 -arch=sm_90 -lcudart -lcublas -Xcompiler -fPIC` for both; Triton built with default CUDA_TOOLKIT=12.2. Also kernel selector: `prefer_triton=true` in runtime config for these experiments.
maria: Any KV cache/paging interaction? Paged attention path can trigger extra device-host copies which look like kernel regressions.
devon: Good call — we saw extra memcpy spikes in the paged path when using Triton. Example from perf trace (ns):
```
[PROFILE] kernel_attention_triton: 12000000 ns
[PROFILE] kernel_attention_cuda: 8200000 ns
[PROFILE] kv_page_commit memcpy H2D: 1800000 ns
[PROFILE] kv_page_evict memcpy D2H: 2400000 ns
```
devon: The triton variant seems to interact poorly with our KV page commit timing, causing overlapping memcpys that serialize more than on the cuda kernel.

infra-bot: CI perf job queued: run/1782047 — microbench + nvprof attached (artifact).
sasha: Can you run the microbench with `--no-paginate-kv` and `--batch_policy=tokens`? Need to isolate whether it's pure compute kernel vs paging+batching heuristic.
devon: Ran that — with `--no-paginate-kv` Triton performance moves up to ~920 tps for seq=4096 (vs 760), still ~6% behind CUDA. So paging is majority cause but not all.

omar: Interesting. Also check SM efficiency and achieved occupancy from the profiler. Triton kernels sometimes generate loops that don't vectorize well for long KV strides on sm90.
devon: Profiler summary (Nsight):
```
impl,triton
sm_efficiency,65%
warp_efficiency,84%
achieved_occupancy,0.45

impl,cuda
sm_efficiency,80%
warp_efficiency,92%
achieved_occupancy,0.72
```
sasha: That sm_eff drop explains much. Suggest adding a kernel-selector rule: for sm90 + seq>=2048 prefer cuda_fused_attention until we root cause. I'll open a quick PR to gate `prefer_triton` behind an arch+seq heuristic. :hammer_and_wrench:
devon: I'll attach full nvprof traces to the PR and a minimal reproducer for CI. Also adding a perf regression test in our perf-suites that runs seq=4096 on sm90 images.
maria: Long-term we should investigate whether Triton codegen assumptions (shared memory usage / block sizing) need adjustment for sm90's L2/shared balance. Could be that tunables need to be regenerated with `--triton-tune` for sm90.
omar: Agreed. Also add a quick check to the compile matrix: triton with `--cuda-gencode=sm_90` vs sm_80 and compare PTX outputs; differences in loop unrolling may be telling.
sasha: I'll coordinate the PR + perf test. devon, can you paste the `kernel_selector.conf` snippet you used?
devon: Here it is:
```
{"selector": [
  {"impl":"triton","min_seq":0,"max_seq":2048},
  {"impl":"cuda","min_seq":2049,"max_seq":99999}
]}
```
sasha: Thanks. I'll land a slightly stricter rule: prefer cuda for seq>=2048 on sm90 in the staging rollout.

devon: One more note — the regression only shows up with `--batch_policy=dynamic` (we use token-aware batching). With fixed batch size the gap narrows. Something about token packing + triton kernel launch latency is amplifying the effect.
maria: Noted. Let's track this in the attention-portability board and add tickets for: (1) triton tuning for sm90, (2) kernel selector PR, (3) KV paging overlap fix.

sasha: Filed PR #2124 for selector + perf test. Assigned to @devon for artifacts and @omar for triton tuning follow-up. :rocket: 

devon: I'll drop the nvprof tarball in the PR and run on SM80/SM90 nightly matrix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
